title: Which Oklahoma Coaches Are in the College Football Hall of Fame?
question: Which Oklahoma Sooners head football coaches are in the College Football Hall of Fame?
answer: Six former Oklahoma head coaches are enshrined as coaches: Bennie Owen (1951), Lawrence "Biff" Jones (1954), Bud Wilkinson (1969), Jim Tatum (1984), Barry Switzer (2001) and Bob Stoops (2021 class). Gomer Jones, OU's coach in 1964-65, is also in, but as a player.
summary: Six OU head coaches are in the College Football Hall of Fame as coaches: Owen, Biff Jones, Wilkinson, Tatum, Switzer and Stoops. Gomer Jones got in as a player.
body: Oklahoma's coaching tree runs deep in the College Football Hall of Fame. Six men who served as OU head coaches have been inducted as coaches, and together they span more than a century of Sooner football.

The list starts with Bennie Owen, a charter member of the Hall in 1951, who coached the Sooners from 1905 to 1926 and went 122-54-16. Lawrence "Biff" Jones followed in 1954; his OU stay covered just 1935 and 1936, with a 9-6-3 record. Bud Wilkinson, who went 145-29-4 from 1947 to 1963, was inducted in 1969, and Jim Tatum, OU's one-season coach in 1946 who went 8-3, joined in 1984.

The modern era added two more. Barry Switzer, 157-29-4 from 1973 to 1988, was inducted in 2001. Bob Stoops, the program's all-time wins leader, was elected in the 2021 class; SoonerStats lists his OU mark as 191-48, counting his one interim game in 2021.

There is a fun bonus answer, too. Gomer Jones, who succeeded Wilkinson and coached OU in 1964 and 1965, is also in the Hall of Fame. He was inducted in 1978 for his playing career as an All-American center at Ohio State, not for his coaching. So if a trivia question asks how many former OU head coaches are in the Hall, seven is defensible, but six were honored for coaching.
